passage:
A hill in the city was once a landfill. After careful cleaning and covering, it became a park.
Students visiting the park saw grass, trees, and walking paths. Then the guide showed old photos of trash piles. The contrast was shocking.
The park had special systems to manage gas and water under the ground. It looked natural, but it required engineering.
Students learned that repair can transform damaged land, but the past does not disappear completely.
The park was hopeful, not simple. It showed that human mistakes can sometimes be managed and healed, but only through long-term responsibility.
